newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Futures Exchange 1996 trade volume up 13.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: HK Futures Exchange 1996 trade volume up 13.9 pct.

text.p: The Hong Kong Futures Exchange Ltd said on Thursday total trading volume on the exchange rose to 5.95 million contracts in 1996, up 13.9 percent over 1995.

Its flagship product, Hang Seng Index (HSI) futures, accounted for 78.3 percent of total turnover last year with 4.66 million contracts traded, up 2.4 percent from 1995, Ivers Riley, chief executive of the HKFE told a news conference.

HSI options recorded impressive growth of 69.5 percent in 1996 to 1.09 million contracts and rolling forex, a currency futures product launched in November 1995, had 195,355 contracts traded in 1996, he said.
But individual stock futures launched in March 1995 had not been successful in 1996. "Turnover is close to zero and daily volume is under one contract," Riley said.
He said the major problem with stock futures was the lack of market makers, and traders had difficulties finding counterparts to match orders.
"A review suggested that a market maker system and a shift from open outcry trading to the electronic Automated Trading System might rectify this," Riley said.
Currently only one member has signed up as a market maker and the new changes will be implemented on February 14, he said.
